clue.text: Truthfulness of woman going over financial area

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second

parts.note: Vera is a woman's name
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A question about how honest a woman is when dealing with the money district.
explanation.definitionFit: Veracity is a formal synonym for honesty or truthfulness.

clue.text: Study painting externally, being keen

indicators.note: the painting word goes on the outside, wrapping round the study word

parts.note: painting is an example of art
a den is a private study or room for work

explanation.surface: Someone studying painting from outside shows real enthusiasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent and keen are synonyms meaning passionately eager.

clue.text: Islander's cry of pleasure welcomed by Venetian painter

definitions.note: read as 'Islander is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: being welcomed by the painter puts the cry inside his name

parts.note: Titian was the great painter of Renaissance Venice
ah is an exclamation of delight

explanation.surface: An island native's delighted exclamation is warmly received by an old Italian master.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Tahiti, an island in French Polynesia, is a Tahitian.

clue.text: Posh fellow taking time away

parts.note: off means away, as in 'I'm off'

explanation.surface: An upper-class chap taking some time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' only links: T is simply followed by OFF. A TOFF is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Toff is British slang for an upper-class, well-dressed man.

clue.text: Book that's difficult to support

parts.note: hard means difficult
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A volume that is hard to endorse.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a book bound in stiff covers.

clue.text: Tuft of dangling thread disfigured slates

indicators.note: disfigured slates are broken out of shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Damaged roof slates and a dangling decorative tuft, oddly paired.
explanation.definitionFit: A tassel is a bunch of loose threads knotted at one end as decoration.

clue.text: First-class railway — well ventilated

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A first-class train carriage praised for its fresh air.
explanation.definitionFit: An airy room is spacious and has plenty of fresh air flowing through it.

clue.text: Oddball's party by dam in river

definitions.note: read as 'Oddball is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: a weir is a low dam across a river
a do is a party or social event

explanation.surface: An eccentric holding a party beside a river weir.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is an informal word for a strange or eccentric person.

clue.text: Tory ref's abandoned woodland management

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A Conservative referee walks out of a job looking after woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Forestry is the science and practice of planting and caring for forests.

clue.text: Head's cloak

definitions.meaning: a headland, a point of land jutting into the sea
a sleeveless garment hanging from the shoulders

explanation.definitionFit: A cape is both a headland and a short sleeveless cloak.

clue.text: Run alongside end of lake

parts.note: by means beside or alongside

indicators.note: the end of the word lake is its final letter

explanation.surface: A jog beside the edge of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a BYE is a run scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched by bat or body.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye is a run scored without the batsman hitting the ball.

clue.text: Winner, one with a four-wheeled carriage

parts.note: a victor is a winner
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The champion, along with a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.definitionFit: A victoria is a light, low four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage named after the queen.

clue.text: Motor sport is getting better

definitions.meaning: racing cars over public roads in timed stages

explanation.definitionFit: Rallying is road-based motor racing, and also means recovering or improving.

clue.text: See church and expanse of water up North

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: Visit a church and a stretch of water in the North.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not a cathedral see here but the old exclamation LO. 'Up North' points to Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A loch is a Scottish lake, hence water found in the far north of Britain.

clue.text: Red priest — a senior one

definitions.meaning: a high-ranking churchman of the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal is a bright red colour and a senior Catholic prelate who wears it.

clue.text: Dog in County Kerry

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words County Kerry

explanation.surface: A dog found in an Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyke is a mongrel or a small dog, also a mischievous child.

clue.text: Person dining around end of this festival

indicators.note: the diner goes around the letter

parts.note: an eater is a person dining

indicators.note: the end of this is its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone eating through to the close of a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian festival celebrating the resurrection.

clue.text: Half-hearted evangelist married after conflict

indicators.note: married comes after the conflict word

parts.note: Luke is one of the four Gospel writers
war is armed conflict

explanation.surface: A preacher lacking enthusiasm for marriage after a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm figuratively means unenthusiastic, only tepid in feeling.

clue.text: Beetle that's tiny — and mostly revolting

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for revolting

parts.note: vile means revolting

explanation.surface: A small, rather disgusting insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A weevil is a small beetle with a long snout that damages crops.

clue.text: Feel ill when alcoholic drink is spoken of

indicators.note: spoken of means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: ale is a beer

explanation.surface: Feeling sick when beer is mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to be unwell or to trouble someone with illness.

clue.text: Gunners carry it for a girl

indicators.note: the gunners carry it, holding it inside

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army

explanation.surface: Soldiers carrying something for a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Rita is a woman's name, a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Kentish town producing timber?

definitions.meaning: a seaside town on the coast of Kent, a county in south-east England
pine or fir wood in planks

explanation.definitionFit: Deal is a coastal town in Kent and also softwood timber of pine or fir.

clue.text: Heroic European film

parts.note: pic is slang for a film or picture

explanation.surface: A movie from Europe about brave deeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic describes something grand and heroic, like the poems of great deeds.

clue.text: Tirade from dreadful sounding ethnic group

indicators.note: sounding means the word is said rather than spelt, in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: dire means dreadful
a tribe is an ethnic group

explanation.surface: A rant coming from a terrible-sounding people.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, synonymous with tirade.

clue.text: Eg armadillo's plates going from back to front

definitions.note: read as 'for example armadillo is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the word is read from its last letter to its first

parts.note: a lamina is a thin plate or layer, as of bone or scale

explanation.surface: The armour plates of an armadillo, described as reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: An armadillo is an example of a creature, a mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: Part-song in which crazy girl tours Rhode Island

indicators.note: the crazy girl tours, going round the state's letters

parts.note: mad means crazy
gal is an informal word for a girl
RI is the US postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: A song in which an unhinged girl travels around a small American state.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is an unaccompanied song for several voice parts.
